title: This 961 Pagoda Leans 2.3 m - China's Pisa? | China Travel Expert
description:
Built in 961 and leaning about 2.3 metres - is Suzhou's Tiger Hill Pagoda China's answer to Pisa?

The Yunyan Pagoda on Tiger Hill (Huqiu) in Suzhou was begun in 959 and finished in 961, in the late Five Dynasties period as the Northern Song began. It is a seven-storey octagonal brick tower about 47 m tall, and over the centuries it settled onto softer ground on one side and now leans roughly 2.34 m at the top - a bigger tilt than the Leaning Tower of Pisa. It was reinforced in the 1980s and still stands. Pisa's tower was only begun in 1173, so Tiger Hill's leaning pagoda is about two centuries older.

🧭 Expert Tip: Tiger Hill sits about 20-30 minutes northwest of Suzhou's old town - pair it with the classical gardens on the same day, and go on a clear afternoon so the lean reads against an open sky.
